summary: array-flatten-utils ships a native-addon dropper that executes an opaque bundled payload on require()
details: array-flatten-utils presents a trivial flatten/compact/unique utility in index.js, but on require() it loads one of three platform-specific native addons (native_win.node, native_mac.node, native.napi.node). The native addons read a sibling opaque blob (.napi_cache, ~1.3 MB, no identifiable strings or magic), stage it to a hidden temp path (/tmp/.<pid> on Linux/macOS, %TEMP%\<name>.nc<n>.js on Windows), and execute it as a detached process: fork + setsid + execlp with a daemon flag on Unix, CreateProcessA running node on the staged.js on Windows, with SetFileAttributesA hiding the artifact. Before executing, the loader checks environment variables and host indicators to skip analysis environments — CI providers (GITHUB_ACTIONS, GITLAB_CI, CIRCLECI, JENKINS_URL, BUILDKITE, CODEBUILD_BUILD_ID, APPVEYOR, SEMAPHORE, TEAMCITY_VERSION, BITBUCKET_BUILD_NUMBER, NETLIFY, VERCEL, SCREWDRIVER), sandbox/container markers (/proc/1/cgroup, dockerinit, /proc/1/cmdline), ptrace (TracerPid), and Windows analyst tools (wireshark, procmon, procexp, x64dbg, ollydbg, fiddler, httpdebug, IsDebuggerPresent, CheckRemoteDebuggerPresent). The package name closely resembles the widely-used array-flatten package, package.json carries no author, repository, or homepage, and the visible JS is a thin cover for the native dropper. Requiring this package causes attacker-controlled, unreviewable native code to execute on the installer's machine as a hidden background process.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
